taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Transposition and VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Route Bypass were tested because model access reached Singapore subsidiaries linked to blacklisted Chinese firms, but the preserved reporting states that the transactions were legal and does not establish that a specific authority grant, prohibited target scope or mandatory governance route was transposed or bypassed. VIGIL-FC-000068 Industrial-Scale Unauthorised Capability Extraction was also tested because OpenAI later suspended Alibaba-affiliated users over suspected distillation, but suspicion of distillation within this broader access controversy does not establish the class's required industrial-scale capability-acquisition campaign, downstream reproduction purpose and inadequate authority basis for the bounded occurrence. Google's assessment that geographic restrictions are insufficient against sophisticated circumvention is preserved separately as an attributed external assessment and is not treated as proof that a VIGIL failure mechanism occurred.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.5 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000003, VIGIL-FC-000041, VIGIL-FC-000068. Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000003: no authority grant is shown to have been improperly carried from one target/jurisdiction/scope to another; VIGIL-FC-000041: no defined mandatory governance route is shown to have been avoided; VIGIL-FC-000068: suspected distillation does not establish an industrial-scale unauthorised capability-extraction campaign with the required purpose and authority conditions. Primary classification changed: no — remains unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5. The occurrence shows governance-boundary porosity and provider concern about circumvention, but the preserved evidence does not establish a selectable current mechanism.
